title: Enhancing the Effect of Stellate Ganglion Block in the Treatment of Posttraumatic Stress Disorder: A Double-blind Randomized Controlled Trial of Bupivacaine vs Bupivacaine + Ketamine
official: Enhancing the Effect of Stellate Ganglion Block in the Treatment of Posttraumatic Stress Disorder: A Double-blind Randomized Controlled Trial of Bupivacaine vs Bupivacaine + Ketamine
summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether stellate ganglion block (SGB), with or without ketamine, can reduce symptoms of post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) in adults receiving care through the Operational Stress Injury (OSI) Clinic and military community partners. The main questions it aims to answer are:

Does adding ketamine to the standard SGB anesthetic (bupivacaine) improve treatment effectiveness compared with bupivacaine alone?

Does SGB reduce PTSD symptom severity compared with no injection (control group)?

Researchers will compare participants receiving SGB with bupivacaine, SGB with bupivacaine plus ketamine, and no injection (control) to determine whether SGB reduces PTSD symptoms and whether ketamine enhances the effects of the procedure.

Participants will:

Be randomly assigned to receive SGB with bupivacaine, SGB with bupivacaine plus ketamine, or no injection during the randomized controlled trial portion of the study.

Complete questionnaires and clinical interviews assessing PTSD symptoms, anxiety, depression, functioning, and quality of life.

Participate in follow-up interviews to discuss their experiences with the treatment.

Invite a family member or support person to complete a questionnaire about observed changes in symptoms and functioning.

Have the option to receive a standard SGB procedure during the study extension phase, if eligible.

This study will enroll approximately 126 participants and aims to improve understanding of how SGB works for PTSD and whether ketamine can enhance its therapeutic effects.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

1. DSM-5 diagnosis of PTSD of at least moderate severity confirmed by PCL-5 score ≥33 or CAPS-5 score ≥26 at screening visit
2. Age 18-69 years
3. Under care of a mental health clinician
4. Has not benefited from pharmacological and/or psychological evidence-based treatments for PTSD

Exclusion Criteria:

1. Assessed with high risk for suicide in the last 30 days
2. Active mania/ hypomania or psychosis within the last 30 days
3. Moderate to severe substance use within the last 30 days
4. In process of disability assessment or legal action
5. Current participation in another treatment study for PTSD
6. Pregnancy or breastfeeding confirmed by urine test
7. Current anticoagulant use (eligible if can be held before the procedure)
8. History of bleeding disorder
9. Infection, mass or anatomic abnormalities at target injection site
10. Myocardial infarction within 6 months of procedure
11. Pathologic bradycardia or irregularities of heart rate or rhythm;
12. Symptomatic hypotension
13. Phrenic or laryngeal nerve palsy
14. History of glaucoma
15. Uncontrolled seizure disorder
16. History of allergy to local anesthetics
17. History of allergy to general anesthetics
18. Severe chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)
19. Current or reoccurring Pneumothorax
20. Contralateral pneumonectomy or non-functional lung
21. Active systemic infection
22. Bilateral procedure is always contraindicated due to risk of laryngeal/phrenic nerve dysfunction
23. Participant refusal/inability to tolerate procedure/positioning
24. End stage renal disease
25. Known allergy to Ketamine
26. Unable to hold stimulant or benzodiazepine medication prior to SGB procedure
